newsitem.title: UK: Police arrest woman after Conservative bomb scare.
newsitem.headline: Police arrest woman after Conservative bomb scare.

text.p: Police said on Thursday they had arrested a local woman after a bomb scare near the ruling Conservative party's annual conference.
A police spokesman from this southern coastal resort town said bomb squad officers had been called after a suspicious package was found near the conference centre.
The package was found to be a "non-viable device", he said. Device is a word police commonly use to describe a bomb.
The spokesman said a 45-year-old local woman was arrested and was in custody. He said no further details would be given.
Security around the conference centre is extremely tight, with every visitor searched, police ringing the site and marksmen from the security services on rooftops.

The annual conferences have been heavily policed since an Irish Republican Army guerrilla bomb devastated the Grand Hotel in Brighton during the party's 1984 conference. The then prime minister Margaret Thatcher narrowly escaped with her life.
Security has been stepped up since the IRA staged a double car bomb attack at Britain's army headquarters in Northern Ireland on Monday, wounding 31 people.
